name: Mississippi River
hook: One river, sixteen clues: its course, its cities and the war that made its bluffs famous.

facts.label: its course
facts.statement: The Mississippi rises in Minnesota and runs 2,348 miles to the Gulf of Mexico, draining the nation's midsection.

facts.label: New Orleans
facts.statement: New Orleans is the largest city with parts on both banks of the Mississippi, and in 1861 it was the South's most populous city.

facts.label: St. Louis
facts.statement: St. Louis sits on the Mississippi; Lewis and Clark set out from there in 1804, and its Missouri Gazette was the first newspaper west of the river.

facts.label: La Salle
facts.statement: In 1682 the sieur de La Salle followed the Mississippi to its mouth and claimed the whole valley for France as Louisiana.

facts.label: Vicksburg
facts.statement: Vicksburg, the "Gibraltar of the Confederacy," fell on July 4, 1863; the city did not observe Independence Day again until 1945.

facts.label: the Ws and Ks
facts.statement: For U.S. radio call letters the Mississippi divides most W stations from K stations, and it separates most of the country's east from its west.
